Work in C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod (Next.js 16 + Prisma, an AI website builder called Kodely).

BUILD: expand the asset library with **illustrations and procedural imagery** — the categories that make a generated site stop looking like a wireframe.

## Read the constraint before designing — it rules out the obvious answer
Generated sites run under `default-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'none'` with **no external hosts** and no way to add npm packages. Read `app/api/site/[slug]/[[...path]]/route.ts` and `lib/agent.ts`'s SYSTEM prompt.

Two consequences that decide this task:
1. **Stock photography is impossible.** Not un-built — impossible. No remote host, and a base64 raster passes through the model's context as tokens: a 200 KB PNG is roughly 88,900 tokens, about $1.07 per four-turn build, more than the rest of the build. Do not add raster imagery.
2. **Nothing may be scraped or copied.** Every asset must be your own hand-authored geometry or arithmetically generated. No path data lifted from any icon set, illustration pack or CSS library, free or licensed — these get inlined into customers' commercial sites, so an unlicensed asset becomes their legal problem. State the provenance of everything you add.

## Read what exists
`lib/assets/icons.ts` (147 icons), `flags.ts`, `patterns.ts` (30 gradients, 6 meshes, 3 grain textures, 12 dividers, 12 CSS patterns, initials avatars), and `index.ts` (the catalogue, `findAssets`, and the DEMONYMS/tie-break logic). **Match their structure exactly** — stable ids, keywords, a `render` that returns paste-ready `source` plus a one-line `usage`.

## Build, in `lib/assets/illustrations.ts`
Aim for things that fill the large empty areas a hero or an empty state leaves, which is where generated sites currently look unfinished:
- **Abstract hero backdrops** — layered blobs, arcs, concentric forms, generated from parameters rather than drawn by hand, so one function yields many variants.
- **Spot illustrations** built from the same geometric vocabulary: a storefront, a cup, a plant, a parcel, a calendar, a location marker, a document, a chat bubble — simple, flat, recognisable at 200px, and consistent with each other.
- **Decorative marks** — underline swashes, highlight strokes, starbursts, arrows, brackets, quote marks.
- **Empty-state and placeholder art**, since generated sites routinely need a "no items yet" panel.
- Anything else in that spirit you can argue for.

**Consistency matters more than count.** Twenty pieces that clearly belong to one family beat sixty that don't. Use a shared stroke weight, corner radius and palette approach, and make them inherit `currentColor` where sensible so they adopt the site's brand.

## Constraints
- **Size is cost.** Report the byte size of what you add and keep individual pieces lean — these are inlined into source files that get re-sent to the model on every turn. Prefer parameterised generators over long literal path data.
- Every piece must render correctly with no external anything, and must work on both light and dark backgrounds or say which it needs.
- Register everything in the catalogue so `findAssets` reaches it, with keywords a non-designer would actually type ("hero background", "empty state", "coffee illustration").
- Scope — ONLY: `lib/assets/illustrations.ts` and `lib/assets/index.ts` (to register). Do NOT edit icons.ts, flags.ts, patterns.ts, lib/agent.ts, or anything under app/.
- No new npm dependencies. Do NOT run `npm run build`, `git commit`, `git push`, or `deploy.sh`.
- **HARD GATE: `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx eslint app lib components`, and `node --import ./scripts/test/register.mjs --test "tests/*.test.mjs"` must ALL pass — currently 0 errors, 0 warnings, 209 tests.** Note `tests/assets.test.mjs` covers `findAssets`; if you change ranking behaviour, update it and say so.
- **Render everything and look at it.** A malformed path renders as a blob and a typecheck will not catch it. Report what you actually inspected versus what you only wrote.

## Report back
What you added with byte sizes and total, the provenance statement, how you kept the family visually consistent, what you rendered and inspected, and any category you concluded is impossible under the CSP.

475	function tokenScore(entry: Entry, token: string, isSynonym: boolean): number {
476	  const bare = entry.id.slice(entry.id.indexOf(":") + 1);
477	  let best = 0;
478	  if (bare === token) best = 16;
479	  else if (entry.name.toLowerCase() === token) best = 14;
480	  else {
481	    for (const kw of entry.keywords) {
482	      if (kw === token) best = Math.max(best, 10);
483	      else if (token.length >= 3 && kw.startsWith(token)) best = Math.max(best, 6);
484	      else if (token.length >= 4 && kw.includes(token)) best = Math.max(best, 3);
485	      if (best === 10) break;
486	    }
487	    if (best === 0 && token.length >= 4 && bare.includes(token)) best = 4;
488	  }
489	  // A synonym hit is real but weaker than the word the caller actually typed.
490	  return isSynonym ? best * 0.6 : best;

505	/**
506	 * Keyword/synonym search across icons, flags, gradients, meshes, textures,
507	 * dividers, patterns and avatars.
508	 *
509	 * Multi-word queries are AND-ish: every token must contribute something, so
510	 * "coffee shop" prefers assets that speak to both rather than everything that
511	 * mentions "shop". An empty query lists the catalogue (filtered by `kind`).
512	 */
513	export function findAssets(query: string, opts: FindAssetsOptions = {}): AssetMatch[] {
514	  const limit = Math.min(Math.max(opts.limit ?? 20, 1), 100);
515	  const allowed = kindFilter(opts.kind);
516	  const pool = allowed ? CATALOG.filter((e) => allowed.has(e.kind)) : CATALOG;
517	
518	  const tokens = tokenize(query);
519	  if (tokens.length === 0) return pool.slice(0, limit).map((e) => toMatch(e, 0, opts));
520	
521	  const scored: { entry: Entry; score: number; matched: number }[] = [];
522	  for (const entry of pool) {
523	    let total = 0;
524	    let matched = 0;
525	    for (const token of tokens) {
526	      let best = tokenScore(entry, token, false);
527	      if (best === 0) {
528	        for (const syn of SYNONYMS[token] ?? []) {
529	          best = Math.max(best, tokenScore(entry, syn, true));
530	        }
531	      }
532	      if (best > 0) {
533	        matched++;
534	        total += best;
535	      }
536	    }
537	    // PREFER assets that match every token; do not REQUIRE it.
538	    //
539	    // This used to drop any entry that missed a single token, which made the
540	    // docstring above false and — worse — made its own example return nothing:
541	    // "coffee shop" found no coffee icon, because the coffee icon carries no
542	    // "shop" keyword and the AND threw it away. A search that returns an empty
543	    // list when a perfectly good match exists is the failure mode that sends
544	    // the model back to hand-writing SVG.
545	    //
546	    // Ranking by matched-token COUNT first preserves the intent: an asset that
547	    // speaks to both words still beats one that speaks to either.
548	    if (matched > 0) scored.push({ entry, score: total, matched });
549	  }
550	
551	  scored.sort(
552	    (a, b) =>
553	      b.matched - a.matched ||
554	      b.score - a.score ||
555	      // Tie-break on the shorter NAME, not the id. Score ties are common
556	      // between a country and a territory that contains its demonym, and
557	      // alphabetical order resolved them by luck: it happened to favour France
558	      // over French Guiana, but favoured American Samoa over the United States.
559	      // The shorter name is the more canonical entity.
560	      a.entry.name.length - b.entry.name.length ||
561	      a.entry.id.localeCompare(b.entry.id),
562	  );
563	  return scored.slice(0, limit).map(({ entry, score }) => toMatch(entry, score, opts));
564	}

342	export type DividerRenderOptions = {
343	  /** Fill of the divider shape — normally the colour of the *next* section. */
344	  fill?: string;
345	  /** Rendered height in px (the shape stretches to the container's width). */

352	/**
353	 * A full-bleed `<svg>` divider. Drop it at the very bottom of a section with
354	 * the *following* section's background colour as `fill`.
355	 */
356	export function dividerSvg(id: string, opts: DividerRenderOptions = {}): string | null {
357	  const preset = DIVIDERS.find((d) => d.id === id);
358	  if (!preset) return null;
359	  const { fill = "currentColor", height = 90, flipX = false, flipY = false, className } = opts;
360	  const sx = flipX ? -1 : 1;
361	  const sy = flipY ? -1 : 1;
362	  const tx = flipX ? 1440 : 0;
363	  const ty = flipY ? 120 : 0;
364	  const transform = flipX || flipY ? ` transform="translate(${tx} ${ty}) scale(${sx} ${sy})"` : "";
365	  // `block w-full` rather than an inline style: a style attribute is a string
366	  // in HTML but must be an object in JSX, so it would break the moment the
367	  // markup is pasted into a .tsx file. `display:block` matters here — an
368	  // inline svg otherwise sits on the text baseline and leaves a gap under the
369	  // divider.
370	  const cls = `${className ? className + " " : ""}block w-full`;
371	  return (
372	    `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="${DIVIDER_VIEWBOX}" preserveAspectRatio="none"` +
373	    ` width="100%" height="${height}" aria-hidden="true" class="${cls}">` +
374	    `<path d="${preset.d}" fill="${fill}"${transform}/></svg>`
375	  );
376	}

## What I added

**`C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\lib\assets\illustrations.ts`** (new, 36,826 bytes) — 41 catalogue entries across four new kinds, plus the generator machinery.

| Kind | Count | Emitted source, all entries | Largest single piece |
|---|---|---|---|
| `backdrop` (hero backdrops) | 10 | 12,364 B | topo 2,918 B |
| `illustration` (spots) | 12 | 8,005 B | plant 740 B |
| `mark` (decorative) | 11 | 3,239 B | sparkle-trio 565 B |
| `empty-state` | 8 | 5,286 B | load-error 704 B |
| **Total** | **41** | **28,985 B** | avg 707 B |

**`C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\lib\assets\index.ts`** (edited, +~4.4 KB) — four kinds appended to `AssetKind`/`ASSET_KINDS`, catalogue entries with `render`/`usage`/`variants`, re-exports, and a header note on why photography is absent. Because `lib/agent.ts` builds the `find_assets` tool's `kind` enum from `ASSET_KINDS`, the new kinds reach the model without touching agent.ts. Catalogue total went 461 → 502.

- **Backdrops** are parameterised generators (`blobs, rings, arcs, waves, burst, topo, confetti, orbit, hills, spotlight`) on a 1200×600 slice canvas, driven by FNV-1a → mulberry32. Every entry ships a second `seeded` variant, so three sections can share one backdrop without looking cloned; output is deterministic across rebuilds (verified).
- **Spots**: storefront, cup, plant, parcel, calendar, marker, document, chat, bag, house, truck, toolbox.
- **Marks**: 3 underlines, marker highlight, circled emphasis, sparkle, sparkle trio, 2 arrows, brackets, quote marks.
- **Empty states**: no-items, no-results, no-messages, empty-cart, load-error, all-done, image-placeholder, coming-soon — each with a caption string and a baked-colour `dataUri` variant.

## Provenance

Every coordinate is original. Hand-placed primitives (lines, arcs, circles, rounded rects) on a 120-unit grid, plus paths computed at render time from sine terms and a seeded PRNG. Nothing was copied, traced or adapted from any icon set, illustration pack, CSS library or template, free or licensed. Stated in the file header.

## How the family holds together

One pen (`currentColor`, stroke-width 4, round cap/join, 120-unit height, no second weight, no hand-drawn corner radii — the round join *is* the radius). One accent: a single blob at 13% `currentColor` behind each spot and empty state, generated by the *same* `blobPath` function that draws the hero backdrops. No literal colour anywhere unless the caller passes one, so everything inherits brand colour and works light-on-dark and dark-on-light. Common ground line at y=100. The "no items" open box and the parcel are deliberately the open/closed twins of one isometric construction.

## What I rendered and inspected

All 41, in a browser, at ~120–240 px, on white and on `#0b1120`, plus backdrops at a second seed and marks composited under live text. The Browser pane wouldn't composite frames (contended by other sessions on this machine), so after the first pass I rasterised the live SVGs through the page's own canvas and read the PNGs back. Five things were only found by looking:

- **house** — door/window/chimney read as floating rectangles; rebuilt symmetric with a centred door and a round gable window.
- **parcel** — a flat rect with a lid line and a full-height tape reads as a *window pane*; rebuilt isometric.
- **coming-soon** — cone too narrow to read; widened.
- **waves** — four layers at 0.16 opacity stacked to near-solid; lightened.
- **sparkle-trio** — the corner-rounding stroke made the small sparkles blobby; 3 → 2.

Also trimmed topo and confetti for size (topo 3,804 → 2,918 B, keeping the 10-point sampling that is the whole reason it reads as contours rather than rings).

Not inspected pixel-by-pixel: the `dataUri` variants (verified programmatically to contain no `currentColor`, which cannot resolve inside one).

## Gate

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean · `npx eslint app lib components` exit 0, **0 errors 0 warnings** · `node --import ./scripts/test/register.mjs --test "tests/*.test.mjs"` **303/303 pass**. No test changes were needed — I didn't touch ranking, only added entries. Note the counts moved under me: baseline was 209 when I started, and other sessions added `tests/build-diff.test.mjs` and extended `site-seo.test.mjs` while I worked (they also cleared five pre-existing PromptWizard lint warnings). `tests/assets.test.mjs` iterates `ASSET_KINDS`, so its CSP/JSX/uniqueness assertions now cover the new kinds automatically.

Extra checks: no new source references a remote host; no kebab-case attribute survives into a `jsx` source (illustrations use `stroke-dasharray`, which `toJsx` in icons.ts doesn't cover, so `illustrations.ts` carries its own extended converter rather than editing icons.ts); backdrops byte-identical across repeated renders.

## Impossible under the CSP

- **Stock photography** — no remote host, and a base64 raster is a context-cost catastrophe, as the brief says. Not attempted.
- **Raster textures of any kind** (paper scans, fabric, bokeh) — same reason. The existing `feTurbulence` grain in patterns.ts is the only honest substitute and it already exists.
- **Web-font-based decorative lettering** — the CSP sets no `font-src`, so fonts fall to `default-src 'self'`, which excludes `data:`. A base64 font is blocked exactly like a remote one, so anything needing a display face has to be drawn as paths.
- **Animated/interactive illustration relying on external runtimes** (Lottie, GSAP) — no packages, no CDN. Pure CSS/SMIL animation would be possible but I left it out; it fights `prefers-reduced-motion` and adds bytes for little gain at this stage.

One judgement call worth flagging: I used four kinds rather than one `illustration` kind, matching the existing granularity (gradient/mesh/texture/divider/pattern are all separate). It widens the `find_assets` enum from 8 to 12 values.
